name: NERVE WARS: BCI Reflex Championship Open
description: NERVE WARS is the largest open-entry BCI reflex competition in the Great Lakes corridor, structured as a tiered elimination tournament testing reaction time, signal precision, multi-channel processing, and neural endurance across standardized hardware-agnostic protocols. Unlike corporate neural leagues that require proprietary BCI systems, NERVE WARS accepts any certified BCI model, making it theoretically accessible across all economic tiers — though the performance gap between a Shelf-grade consumer BCI and a Tier 4 custom neural array is statistically significant and widely discussed. The tournament is broadcast on both standard and neural-sync feeds, with the neural broadcast giving viewers a diluted version of the competitor's own reflex experience.
story_hooks: A NERVE WARS competitor with a decade-old budget BCI begins qualifying above her statistical ceiling — and the hardware audit reveals her BCI has been remotely upgraded by an unknown party with unclear motives.
The 2222 tournament's neural-sync feed contains something that is not advertising — a fragmented signal that three separate viewers independently experience as a cry for help.

A NERVE WARS governing council member is approached by a corponation offering full tournament sponsorship in exchange for mandatory BCI brand registration — and the offer comes with an implicit threat about what happens to independent institutions that decline.
